title: journey-qa persona roster
description: A fictitious team. Every value is invented; nothing is derived from real people or real data.

privileged_roles.description: Roles that count as privileged (roster_check --admins, sql_assert kind privileged_handle). Default ["admin"].

id.description: Stable key used by scenarios (persona: ivy).

name.description: Display name. Must be obviously fictitious.

email.description: Product login email. Reserved domain only (example.com/.org/.net or .test/.example). .invalid is kept for must-fail test fixtures.

handle.description: OS user name / product user id. Allowed by the HOMEPATH rule.

role.description: Product role, in the product's stored shape (adapter defines allowed values).

persona.description: Behavioural profile used by journeys and the data generator.

experience.description: Perspective: how familiar the person is with this kind of product. Decides which steps they find obvious and which they get stuck on.

device.description: Perspective: what the person uses. A scenario can derive browser emulation from it (personas[].emulation.from_roster).

assistive_tech.description: Perspective: assistive technology or input mode the person depends on. A barrier met on the journey is a journey defect. A scenario can emulate zoom and reduced-motion; the others are driven by whoever runs the journey.

reads_docs.description: Perspective: how the person uses the public documentation. Decides which documented steps they perform as written.

language.description: Perspective: BCP 47 tag of the language the person reads and writes in (for example en-US).

goals.description: Perspective: what the person is trying to get done. Written as outcomes, not as steps.

constraints.description: Perspective: what limits the person (time, network, permissions, prior tools).

accounts.description: Optional extension: external accounts the person uses inside the product. If a person holds external accounts, uniqueness holds per provider: 1:1:1 (person : login_email : account_id).

plan.description: Stored-shape value the product writes, never a display label.

cwd.description: Optional extension: working directory. When present it must live under /home/<owner handle>/ or /Users/<owner handle>/.
